findings.claim: mini-install-scope only checks current pack skill names, so stale mini skill copies are missed on full-pack machines despite the spec requiring any mini copy to fail.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion/spec: “When the full pack is present, `mini-install-scope` SHALL `fail` if any mini skill copy exists under either home skills root.” The implementation gets `const names = listSkillNames();` and only probes `path.join(home, root, 'skills', name)` for those names, so a removed/renamed mini skill directory under `<home>/.claude/skills` or `<home>/.agents/skills` is never examined.
findings.suggested_fix: When full pack is present, scan both home skill roots for all installed directories and identify mini-owned copies by a durable marker or manifest, rather than limiting the search to the current `skills/` directory names.

findings.claim: mini-kbd-state invokes a different command shape than the specified canonical `prometheus kbd status --json`, causing the CLI to be treated as unavailable even when it is on PATH.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria task 2.1 specifies `mini-kbd-state` as “(`prometheus kbd status --json` resolves or the waypoint projection parses; never both disagreeing)”, but the implementation spawns `prometheus` with `['kbd', '--path', repoRoot, 'status', '--json']`; the pasted 4.1 evidence in tasks.md simultaneously reports the prometheus CLI is on PATH and `mini-kbd-state` warns “The prometheus CLI is not available,” which is consistent with invoking the wrong subcommand shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Spawn the documented command shape, e.g. `['kbd', 'status', '--json']` plus any path option only in a CLI-supported position, and include stderr in the warning detail when the command exists but exits nonzero.

findings.claim: A home skill file that is a symlink to byte-identical content is accepted as matching, so the check can report pass while the installed copy is not actually a copy.
findings.evidence: The requirement says `copy-skills` SHALL “copy — never symlink,” but `differs()` uses `statSync(b).isFile()` and `readFileSync(b)`, both of which follow symlinks; if `<home>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is a symlink to a file with the same bytes as the pack source, `differs()` returns false and `drift()` reports no problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `lstatSync` on destination files and treat symbolic links as drift so `copy-skills` replaces them with regular files.
